newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down on Friday due to weak sentiment on the domestic A share market, which prevented investors from borrowing on the repo market, traders said.
Turnover fell to 6.70 million lots from 8.67 million on Thursday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.19 percent from 11.99 percent.
"The A share market was still dull, although it closed up today," said one trader. "With investor confidence weak, institutional borrowing fell on the repo market."
Traders said early-maturing contracts lost less than late-maturing contracts, with some investors borrowing shorter-term funds to prepare for an A share isssue on Monday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed mostly up due to a technical rebound, traders said.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market shrank to 1.67 million lots from 1.78 million.
The 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 was the most active and ended up at 121.33 yuan from 120.57.
"Technical charts showed the contract hit the bottom yesterday and began to rebound today," said one trader.
"The spot contracts might climb up slightly next week after sharp falls earlier this month," said a second trader.
"But the present high levels of the repo rates will be a negative factor preventing the spots from rising sharply," he added.
